actions.newValue: Henry Finn, a tech billionaire and boss of the electric car company Edison Motors, travels to Bolivia to buy the land of Kimsa, who lives in an abandoned train on a salt flat and cares for his sick daughter. Beneath the land lies much of the world's lithium, which a British doctor, Anna, believes could radically improve mental health, and Al Smith's play asks how far people will go for the greater good.

actions.newValue: Pablo Manzi's play takes the audience to a series of locations across Latin America, including Peru, Chile and Mexico, where each new scene brings another horror. Absurdist in tone and oblique in structure, it explores violence and what it takes to build a community, from a nightclub doorway to two guards waiting on the Chilean border.

actions.newValue: Adapted from Andrea Levy's novel, the play follows two women whose lives collide in 1948 London: Hortense, a Black teacher who leaves Jamaica, and Queenie, who escapes her parents' butcher business on an English farm. Set around the wartime and post-war treatment of Britain's Black citizens, it traces the families and fractured dreams of the Windrush generation.
actions.description: BRO-6075: backfill empty West End historical synopsis, written from the show's collected review texts

actions.newValue: Six Black British men, named after aspects of blackness such as Jet, Onyx, Obsidian and Sable, meet in what appears to be a therapy session, seated on a line of plastic chairs. Ryan Calais Cameron's choreopoem mixes monologue, movement and music as they open up about racism, police stop-and-search, school, history and what it feels like to be British and Black.
actions.description: BRO-6075: backfill empty West End historical synopsis, written from the show's collected review texts

actions.newValue: David Eldridge's two-hander opens with Maggie telling her husband Gary that she no longer loves him. Approaching 50, trapped in her role as wife and mother and lonely, she longs for the woman she used to be, and the couple face the question of how to tell when a marriage is really over. It is the second play in Eldridge's trilogy, after Beginning.
actions.description: BRO-6075: backfill empty West End historical synopsis, written from the show's collected review texts

actions.newValue: Anupama Chandrasekhar's play is narrated by Nathuram Godse, the man who assassinated Gandhi, and traces how a boy once inspired by the Father of the Nation came to kill him. It sets his ideology against Gandhi's and examines India's internal conflicts.
actions.description: BRO-6075: backfill empty West End historical synopsis, written from the show's collected review texts

actions.newValue: Daniel is a cantankerous patriarch in the last stages of emphysema, whose malice remains undiminished and whose target is his son Michael. Theresa Rebeck's wildly dysfunctional family drama sets the dying father's provocations against a household of bitterly comic quarrels.
actions.description: BRO-6075: backfill empty West End historical synopsis, written from the show's collected review texts

actions.newValue: Jess, who has cerebral palsy, receives a visit from a Department of Work and Pensions assessor and answers every question honestly, only to lose the higher rate of her personal independence payment. Her Motability car is then taken away. Francesca Martinez's play charts the effects of austerity and cuts to adult social care on disabled people.
actions.description: BRO-6075: backfill empty West End historical synopsis, written from the show's collected review texts

actions.newValue: Jack, a 22-year-old volunteer on Switchboard, an LGBT+ phoneline, takes a call one hungover morning from an older man called Michael. Michael tells him the story of what he plans to be his last night on earth, 29 February 1988, a night out in Soho at the height of the AIDS crisis. Jack Holden's one-man show is based on a true story.
actions.description: BRO-6075: backfill empty West End historical synopsis, written from the show's collected review texts

actions.newValue: Set on a stormy night in 1991 on Tuck Island, the drag murder mystery has Lady Von Fistenburg preparing a soiree to celebrate the tenth wedding anniversary of the Prince and Princess of Wales. It is billed as a Dragatha Christie murder mystery, in which things are not always what they seem.
actions.description: BRO-6075: backfill empty West End historical synopsis, written from the show's collected review texts

actions.newValue: Ben and Alex, a struggling double act, are booked as the warm-up for Jimmy and Sid, a once-beloved elderly double act on a comeback tour who have wound up in a regional theatre. When a Hollywood director unexpectedly pops in, the actors get wind of him and the evening descends into chaotic one-upmanship.

actions.newValue: Dylan Thomas's play for voices is staged in the dementia wing of a care home, where a frightened Owain Jenkins tries to reconnect with a father who no longer recognises him. Poetry draws them into the vibrant, magical retelling of a day in a small Welsh town.

actions.newValue: Two young Black Londoners cut a path through the opening day of Notting Hill Carnival in 2017, months after the Grenfell Tower fire. Yasmin Joseph's play mixes comedy, social commentary and dance on the heritage and politics of the street party.

actions.newValue: Cleo and her friend Kara trade ideas for killing Kylie Jenner, after the star is declared the youngest self-made billionaire and praised for claiming Black culture and beauty as her own for profit. Framed and structured as a Twitter thread, Jasmine Lee-Jones's play explores appropriation, cancel culture and how structural racism devalues and fetishises Black women's bodies.

actions.newValue: In the town of Belleville, which is mourning the loss of Prince Charming, his statue is graffitied and the town loses its title as the most beautiful. The townspeople blame the gobby, gothy Cinderella, whose only friend is the misfit Prince Sebastian, Charming's brother, who must now be married off in an extravagant royal wedding.

actions.newValue: Winsome Pinnock's play begins in 2007 with two women debating the achievement of the painter J.M.W. Turner and his painting of a slave ship. Ten actors play 24 roles as present and past collide, in a drama about how artists illuminate, or betray, the world around them.

actions.newValue: Evan is a socially awkward teenager wearing a cast on his broken arm, on which the disaffected Connor once scrawled his name. After Connor's suicide, Connor's family reach out to Evan, and he ends up deceiving them without having set out to. Spreading through the internet and social media, the lie grows far beyond his control.

actions.newValue: Pinter's play examines a love triangle between Emma, who works in the art world, her husband Robert, a publisher, and Emma's lover Jerry, who is also Robert's best friend and a literary agent. Revelations unspool about who knows what and when, as the trio is on stage throughout. The play was inspired by Pinter's own extramarital affair.

actions.newValue: Arthur Miller's 1947 drama centres on Joe Keller, an affable family man whose business made parts for fighter planes. His former colleague Steve languishes in jail for sending out faulty cylinder heads that led to 21 pilots dying, but Joe seems untouched. A family riven by recent grief is haunted by demons from the past.

actions.newValue: Garry Essendine, the vainglorious actor at the centre of Noel Coward's farce, owns 18 dressing gowns and has men and women alike in thrall. All he really wants is to get through the day and night intact.
actions.description: BRO-6075: backfill empty West End historical synopsis, written from the show's collected review texts

actions.newValue: Alexander Zeldin's modern take on Sophocles' Antigone has two sisters return to their old family home on the anniversary of their father's death. They find that their uncle has remodelled the house, and their plans to honour their father turn into a heated argument over what to do with his ashes. The play runs for 80 minutes.
actions.description: BRO-6075: backfill empty West End historical synopsis, written from the show's collected review texts

actions.newValue: This musical nostalgia trip covers the life of the bandleader Glenn Miller, famous for the sound he pioneered with clarinet and saxophone and for vanishing on a flight across the English Channel in 1944 at the age of forty. The production shares the name and much of the ground of the biographical film starring James Stewart.
actions.description: BRO-6075: backfill empty West End historical synopsis, written from the show's collected review texts

actions.newValue: Judy, 38, is offered voluntary redundancy from her job in corporate finance and decides to become a 1950s-style Domestic Goddess, cleaning, baking and ironing while waiting to hand a cocktail to her estate agent husband Johnny each evening. Laura Wade's comedy examines what that retro lifestyle costs the marriage.
actions.description: BRO-6075: backfill empty West End historical synopsis, written from the show's collected review texts

actions.newValue: A man called Alex wakes up on an ordinary day in an ordinary English town and watches the world go by in the town square. Then things turn strange: a history professor is struck by lightning and dies, and Alex and the professor's daughter Sam immediately marry. Rory Mullarkey's surreal play follows them into a world of war and tragicomedy fuelled by ice cream.
